slides.title: The Retail Illusion vs. Institutional Reality

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: Fraud is just phishing calls and isolated incidents affecting naive victims.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: ₹42.35 Lakh Crore is a systemic liquidity drain forcing tighter settlement rules and banking freezes on all retail accounts.

slides.title: The Hidden Cost of Systemic Friction

stat_data.label: Total Global Fraud Loss
stat_data.context: This massive capital extraction forces banks to implement aggressive compliance filters. For the retail trader, this manifests as delayed settlements, unexpected account freezes, and increased transaction costs that erode net portfolio yields.

slides.title: The Mechanism of Capital Extraction
flowchart_data: 1. Organized networks drain liquidity from the retail ecosystem.
2. Regulators respond by tightening KYC and settlement protocols.
3. Retail traders bear the cost through increased friction and platform latency.

slides.title: How Your Yield Quietly Evaporates
slides.card_text: When systemic fraud spikes, the 'cost of trust' rises. Financial institutions pass this burden to retail users via higher platform fees, restricted liquidity windows, and mandatory compliance buffers. You aren't just losing capital to scams; you are losing efficiency to the defensive walls built to stop them.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Execution Rule
slides.card_text: Never execute capital transfers through third-party intermediaries or unverified fintech overlays. To maintain portfolio integrity, mandate direct clearing corporation settlement exclusively through SEBI-registered brokers. If the path between your bank and the exchange is obscured, your capital is at risk.
